fields.narrative_intro: *A paranoid person and a scruffy person discuss the Apple data breach at a data center that has just been declared a crime scene.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
PARANOID PERSON: "Fourteen ex-Apple employees. Fourteen."
SCRUFFY PERSON: "Allegedly."
fields.panel2:
[build]
PARANOID PERSON: "One took screenshots during their job interview."
SCRUFFY PERSON: "During the interview?"
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
PARANOID PERSON: "Multiple others are now emailing OpenAI asking how to return the laptops they just... kept."
SCRUFFY PERSON: "They kept the laptops."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: Both figures stand completely still under the flickering crime-scene tape. A forensics cone sits next to what is clearly an Apple MacBook someone just mailed to the server room in a shoebox.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
SCRUFFY PERSON: "So the cover-up strategy was emailing the company."
PARANOID PERSON: "On the stolen laptop, presumably."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: A whiteboard on the wall reads 'OPERATIONAL SECURITY SEMINAR — CANCELLED' with eleven sticky notes beneath it, each one an Apple logo peeled off a keyboard.]

narrative_summary: The joke pivots on the absurdity that the implicated employees' self-incriminating cleanup move was voluntarily contacting OpenAI to return the Apple hardware they had quietly kept, implying the cover-up was somehow worse than the original act.
rationale: Candidate 1 earns its score through genuine surprise — the button panel (the 'OPERATIONAL SECURITY SEMINAR — CANCELLED' whiteboard with peeled Apple logo stickers) is the only closing beat that doesn't just restate the setup but adds a new absurd layer. The deadpan rhythm also makes the 'on the stolen laptop, presumably' line land harder than any of the competing FedEx jokes.
story_title: Apple says more ex-employees may have taken confidential data to OpenAI
place: at a data center that has just been declared a crime scene
hat_pair: foam pencil worn as a tall pointy hat with a pink eraser tip at the peak
